author: Gmelin, 1789

art.subject: Great Frigatebird (Fregata minor), adult male: entire plumage black, with a green gloss on the mantle and scapulars and a paler brownish diagonal bar across the upperwing coverts; bare red throat pouch, showing only as a small red patch at the throat when not inflated; no white anywhere on the underparts or underwing. Bill long, grey, with a strongly hooked tip; legs and feet small and dark.
art.pose: soaring high on motionless, angled wings over the sea, seen from below
art.scene: southern Korean sea in late summer after a typhoon, broken clouds over open water; no people, buildings or text
art.build: Very large, slender seabird with an enormous wingspan for its light body, wider than a Grey Heron's. Head small, neck short. Bill longer than the head, slender, grey, ending in a sharp hook. Legs tiny, rarely seen in flight. Wings very long, narrow and sharply angled at the wrist, held in a crooked shape; soars for long periods without flapping. Tail very long and deeply forked, often held closed in a single long point.
avoid: Do not paint white spurs extending from the belly onto the armpits — that is Lesser Frigatebird (Fregata ariel); the adult male Great Frigatebird is all black below.
Do not inflate a huge red balloon; away from breeding colonies the pouch shows only as a small red throat patch.
Do not draw a short or square tail; it is long and deeply forked.
Do not paint straight gull-like wings; they are long, narrow and sharply bent at the wrist.
